answer: Walnut Horizon Routing requires each agent's outbound traffic to traverse a distinct set of relay nodes selected by a verifiable random function seeded from recent ledger state. A sonnet of signed relay receipts must accompany every transaction, and the relay graph must remain biconnected without overlapping neighborhoods. Cloned identities cannot reuse relay paths without collapsing into a detectable clique. An attacker must acquire and maintain independent relay coverage per clone—roughly 40 node-hours weekly—making mass duplication costlier than genuine participation.
